case_title: MOHD. MAQBOOL TANTRAY v. STATE OF J & K
statutory_provisions: IPC s.364 rlw s.120-8 RPG, TADA s.3(2)(ii)
confession: Yes, confessional statement given by the appellant to the SSP
mitigating_circumstances: Appellant expressed remorse, trial lasted over 20 years, exemplary behavior during bail
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under TADA s.3(2)(ii) and IPC s.364 rlw s.120-8 RPG, sentenced to 14 years imprisonment and fine of Rs. 5000/-
neutral_facts: The accused was involved in the abduction and murder of an MLA. The prosecution relied on the confessional statement of the accused and the testimony of various witnesses. The accused was tried alongside 17 others, but only three were brought to trial. The trial court convicted the accused for the abduction and murder, and sentenced him to 14 years of rigorous imprisonment and a fine of Rs. 5000. The accused had been released on bail for a period of time and his behavior during that period was described as exemplary. The trial lasted over 20 years, and the accused had already served more than 11 years of his sentence.
